title: VPC Flightdeck: Patchwave rollout runbook and transactional state handoff
creator: Marco Chen
description: Create an operational runbook and automation components (Flightdeck + Patchwave) to perform orchestrated, transactional upgrades for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The goal is zero-downtime schema and runtime upgrades for customer clusters with explicit rollout gates, cohort canaries, and fast rollback paths tied to telemetry thresholds.
background: Customers running Redwood Private require predictable, audited upgrade paths that avoid data divergence and minimize application disruptions. Existing migration tooling handles step execution but lacks a lightweight staging runway for transactional state handoff (KV cache warmers, prefix snapshot transfers) and a clear, ops-friendly runbook for engineers and on-prem site admins.
design_decisions: Use a two-phase 'handoff' approach: 1) stateless binaries + config rollout; 2) transactional state bridge for critical stores (runtime metadata, provisioning records).
Implement Patchwave as a coordinator that composes canary cohorts by region and capacity tier rather than per-host, to align with Dedicated API semantics.
Gate on SLO-preserving metrics (p99 latency, error-rate, KV delta) exposed in the Console before promoting cohorts.
Prefer declarative migration manifests (YAML) consumed by Flightdeck for idempotent runs and repeatability.
Retain a 'fast-fail' rollback token that reverses schema toggles and redirects traffic to previous binary images within 90 seconds where possible.
All automation emits structured telemetry and audit events for compliance and postmortem analysis.
rollout_plan: Preflight: validate manifest + schema compatibility checks with compatibility-simulator
Stage 0 (dry-run): run migrations in a dry environment using flightdeck --dry-run; verify no schema drift
Stage 1 (canary cohort): apply to 2% of hosts (by load profile) for 30 minutes; monitor p99 latency and KV delta
Stage 2 (staged handoff): run transactional state bridge to copy active KV prefixes and start prefix-warmers; confirm cache hit-rate
Stage 3 (regional expansion): expand cohorts in waves (10%, 30%, 60%) with 15m observation windows
Stage 4 (full rollout): push configuration and switch traffic to new runtime; trigger post-rollout diagnostics
rollback_plan: Immediate abort: Flightdeck marks run as aborted and pauses further cohorts
Automated revert: if telemetry breaches thresholds, Patchwave triggers rollback token to reverse schema flag and point routing back to previous images
State reconciliation: run reverse-bridge to reconcile writes captured during handoff; apply compensating transactions if necessary
Outage fallback: if automatic rollback fails after 3 attempts, escalate to on-call and follow manual runbook steps to restore replicas and DNS routing
telemetry_and_observability: Expose deployment-specific tags on metrics: rollout_id, cohort_id, manifest_hash
Dashboards: rollout-health (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, kv-delta, cache-hit-rate)
Traces: sample 1% of requests with rollout_id for root-cause analysis
Audit logs: structured events for each state transition stored for 365 days in compliance storage
Alerting: SLO breach pager if p99 increases by >20% or error-rate >0.5% for 10m
migration_steps: 1. Generate migration manifest (YAML) using migration-tooling with explicit pre/post hooks
2. Run preflight compatibility-simulator against customer snapshot and record results
3. Create rollback token and store in KMS-backed vault
4. Launch Patchwave with flightdeck manifest; start dry-run for health-checks
5. Promote to canary cohort; engage prefix-warmers and KV bridge
6. Monitor telemetry and run automated smoke checks; run schema validator across replicas
7. Expand cohorts per rollout plan; finalize by flipping config flags to enable new behavior
8. Post-rollout verification and release notes generation
preflight_checks: k8s-resources: deploy quotas and images available
network: VPC connectivity checks to control plane and telemetry endpoints
backup: automatic backups completed and verified
acceptance_criteria: Automated run can complete a full staged rollout on internal test clusters without manual intervention
Rollout metrics published to Console with rollout_id tags
Rollback token successfully reverts a canary cohort in <3 minutes in simulated failure
Runbook steps documented and validated by SRE and Solutions teams
Security review completed and audit logs retained per compliance policy

notes: We intentionally decoupled Patchwave (cohort coordinator) from Flightdeck (executor) to allow future reuse for Dedicated and Hosted upgrades.
Next steps: schedule SRE dry-run and a customer pilot with two low-risk on-prem customers in April.
Consider adding a 'pause-on-deploy' flag for manual approvals in highly regulated districts.
